title: Soraine master research bundle
scope: All three supplied research datasets plus reviewed chat science and combined storyboard. This is not an exhaustive NASA archive or an ignition simulator.

read_me.frontend: Use evidence_records for structured results, findings and concept_cards for explanatory text, and sources for citations.
read_me.counting: Records include aggregate endpoints, fits, models and multi-measurement tests. Record count is not experiment count.
read_me.missing_data: Null means not supplied or not applicable, never zero. An extinction outcome is not a measured zero spread rate.
read_me.comparisons: Series names group evidence, but do not by themselves establish comparable test conditions.
read_me.traceability: Contributor archives preserve original content, including superseded estimates. Do not render those originals as current results.
read_me.models: Keep model-derived evidence distinct from experiment-derived evidence; no interpolation into safety ratings.
read_me.portability: Some archived local paths belong to contributors; source URLs are the shared access routes.

findings.statement: For silicone rubber smoke, the arithmetic mean particle diameter was about 227 nm, while almost half the aerosol mass was in particles larger than 1000 nm. A small average size can hide a large share of the smoke mass in bigger particles.
findings.limitations: Literature finding, not a single run. Not an alarm threshold for a habitat.

findings.statement: Materials were heated below ignition; smoke aging ranged 10-1800 s; a substantial portion of particles were below 500 nm. The source smoke-transport model indicates mixing-dominated transport and longer detection delays than under normal gravity.
BASS-II estimated heat release from oxygen consumption using 13.1 kJ per gram of O2; most reported tests were below 100 W.
findings.limitations: Study method and aggregate finding; not a per-test value.

findings.statement: A NASA assessment approved in March 2022 and published in May 2026 reports ISS water-mist and Orion water-spray extinguisher certification at 30% O2 and 10.2 psia. It identifies lower-pressure discharge and higher-oxygen effectiveness concerns. This does not establish qualification at lunar gravity.

NASA's orientation-independent water/nitrogen fine-water-mist extinguisher, rechargeable from onboard supplies, succeeded against open and baffled-enclosure fires in proof-of-concept tests. Potential Earth uses include aircraft and overturned vehicles.

Some materials that do not sustain burning at 1g can burn in microgravity with low-speed flow or in partial gravity. Earlier work suggests a flame-spread peak and minimum oxygen for burning near lunar gravity for certain cases.
findings.limitations: Condition-specific; not a universal curve. Neither paper supports 'Moon is always worst'.

findings.statement: LUCI used an 11-rpm rotating New Shepard vehicle (effective radius 1.22 m) to burn cotton/fiberglass and a 4-mm PMMA rod in air at normal pressure for over 2.5 minutes.
findings.limitations: Coriolis effects; not a lunar-surface test.

findings.title: Earth tests can miss some low-gravity burning conditions
findings.body: BASS-II reported sustained burning of a quarter-inch PMMA rod at 13.6% oxygen in microgravity, compared with a 16% Earth-gravity blowoff limit. The difference is 2.4 percentage points for this rod experiment.
findings.scope: Evidence card only. Different reported endpoints; this is not a universal PMMA threshold or a lunar safety rating. Source slides do not supply the full paired conditions.

concept_cards.statement: A cabin fire requires combustible material, oxygen and sufficient ignition energy. An electrical fault or overheating equipment can supply the heat; changing destination alone does not ignite material.
Orbital microgravity changes buoyant flow. Ventilation influences oxygen supply and smoke transport. Partial-gravity surfaces still have gravity.
Objects float in orbit because they and the spacecraft are in free fall, not because Earth gravity has disappeared.
Spacecraft fire detection concerns both smoke particles and gases; detector response depends on the smoke and its transport.

psi_snapshot.note: Snapshot of PSI Combustion Science classification. NASA partial-gravity research does exist in NTRS; do not claim NASA has never done it.

ntrs_partial_gravity.material: cellulose tissue samples at 1, 2, and 4 cm widths
ntrs_partial_gravity.note: Ranges/conditions are source-level summary; do not create unreported Cartesian combinations or digitize unverified graph values.

material_thresholds_2012.note: Values come from paper Table I. Starred low-g criteria and 1g statistical criteria differ; comparability limitations apply.
material_thresholds_2012.interpretation: Material-specific results are not monotonic with gravity. A lower threshold indicates sustained burning under that study criterion at lower oxygen; it is not ignition probability or universal hazard ranking.

luci.platform: rotating New Shepard sounding rocket simulated lunar gravity
luci.note: Reported fitted flame rates exist for SIBAL and PMMA. Tip, base, and pyrolysis-front metrics are distinct; not an in-situ lunar trial.

findings.statement: For silicone rubber smoke, the arithmetic mean particle diameter was about 227 nm, while almost half the aerosol mass was in particles larger than 1000 nm. A small average size can hide most of the smoke mass in bigger particles.
findings.limitations: Literature finding, not a single run. Not an alarm threshold for a habitat.

findings.statement: Materials were heated below ignition; smoke aging ranged 10-1800 s; a substantial portion of particles were below 500 nm; mixing dominated smoke transport and lengthened detection delays vs normal gravity.
BASS-II estimated heat release from oxygen consumption using 13.1 kJ per gram of O2; most reported tests were below 100 W.
findings.limitations: Study method and aggregate finding; not a per-test value.

findings.statement: ISS water-mist and Orion water-spray extinguishers are certified at 30% O2 and 10.2 psia. Lower pressure can change discharge; higher O2 can reduce extinguishing effectiveness.

NASA's orientation-independent water/nitrogen fine-water-mist extinguisher, rechargeable from onboard supplies, succeeded against open and baffled-enclosure fires in proof-of-concept tests. Potential Earth uses include aircraft and overturned vehicles.

Some materials that do not sustain burning at 1g can burn in microgravity with low-speed flow or in partial gravity. Earlier work suggests a flame-spread peak and minimum oxygen for burning near lunar gravity for certain cases.
findings.limitations: Condition-specific; not a universal curve. Neither paper supports 'Moon is always worst'.

findings.statement: LUCI used an 11-rpm rotating New Shepard vehicle (effective radius 1.22 m) to burn cotton/fiberglass and a 4-mm PMMA rod in air at normal pressure for over 2.5 minutes.
findings.limitations: Coriolis effects; not a lunar-surface test.

tony.report_title: 阶段性方向汇报：以火焰为中心的太空舱消防交互体验
tony.executive_summary: 我们目前建议把项目做成一个以火焰为视觉主角的交互式科学体验。观众从熟悉的地球燃烧情境进入航天器舱内，切换重力与舱内环境，观察周围材料并点开相关实验。体验重点是帮助技术受众理解：地球测试结果为什么不能自动代表月球或火星居住舱，以及设计人员需要继续验证哪些条件。

stage_report.stage: 方向收敛中；尚未进入最终视觉定稿
stage_report.core_thesis: 火焰行为受重力与舱内环境影响；把实验放回居住舱场景，帮助观众理解消防设计为何需要逐项验证。
stage_report.audience: 教授、本科生与研究生、航空航天研究人员和工程师；表达应直观，但证据与限制要达到技术受众标准。
stage_report.user_job: 看见火焰变化，检查周围材料，查看实验条件与来源，并理解这对居住舱设计意味着什么。
stage_report.creative_direction: 以火焰为中心。舱体作为场景和导航；周围物品作为可点击的材料证据入口；数据卡解释测试条件与适用边界。
experience_story: 地球环境：用熟悉的火焰和材料建立基准。
场景转入航天器：火焰保持视觉焦点，环境与重力状态发生切换。
用户探索材料：点击物品查看燃料类型、实验结果、氧气/压力/气流、平台和来源。
用户做预防选择：起火前将易燃物移出舱内或固定收纳。
回到居住舱设计：指出现有证据能支持什么、还需要什么验证。
visual_and_interaction_principles: 主视觉注意力始终落在火焰；周围物品服务于解释，不抢主叙事。
漂浮只用于轨道微重力情境。月球与火星是部分重力，物品应落在地面或表面。
移出/固定物品属于起火前预防，不呈现把燃烧物扔出舱外作为灭火。
